questions.prompt: Bought with your own cash, which of these makes you a part-owner of a company?

options.explanation: Right: a share is a small piece of ownership in a company.
No: a retail forex position is a contract on an exchange rate, not part of a company.
No: a future is a contract on a price, not ownership of any company.

questions.prompt: Illustrative: 0.10 lot EUR/USD (10,000 EUR) at 1.2000, account in USD, leverage 1:30. What does a 1% move against you cost?

options.explanation: No: that is 1% of 1,200, not of the 12,000 USD trade value.
No: that is the margin, 12,000 ÷ 30, not the loss.
Right: 10,000 × 1.2000 = 12,000 USD, and 1% of that is 120 USD, which is 30% of the 400 USD margin.
No: that would be a 10% move.

questions.prompt: Which statement about trading hours is most accurate?

options.text: They depend on the venue, and activity varies within them
options.explanation: Right: hours are set by the exchange or broker, and liquidity rises and falls within them.

options.text: Every one of the five markets trades all day, every day
options.explanation: No: most have closures, and some have long breaks.

options.text: All five markets open and close at exactly the same times
options.explanation: No: hours differ between markets, exchanges and products.

questions.prompt: A fictional stock shows bid 1.00 USD and ask 1.04 USD. You buy 1,000 shares and sell straight away. Ignoring commission, what does the round trip cost?

options.explanation: No: the spread is 0.04 USD on each of 1,000 shares.
No: that is what you paid, not what you lost.
No: that is the spread on one share only.
Right: (1.04 − 1.00) × 1,000 = 40 USD, before price moves at all.

questions.prompt: A friend says: 'Penny stocks are a cheap way to start.' What is the best reply?

options.text: True: a low share price means low risk
options.explanation: No: price per share says nothing about risk.

options.text: Low price is never the same as low risk or cost
options.explanation: Right: thin trading and wide spreads can make them costly and hard to exit.

options.text: True, as long as you buy a lot of shares to spread it out
options.explanation: No: buying more of one thinly traded stock adds to the risk instead of spreading it.

questions.prompt: Which is the best reason to choose a market to study first?

options.text: It is the market most talked about online this month
options.explanation: No: popularity says nothing about whether it fits your time, account or risk.

options.text: A stranger posted a big profit from it online
options.explanation: No: one claimed result is not evidence, and may not be true.

options.text: Its hours and smallest trade size fit your time and risk
options.explanation: Right: fit with your schedule and your risk per trade is a sound starting point.
